The proposal is in `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/25/spawned/mastermind-forms/inapp/proposal.md`.

- **Google sign-in:** it is blocked in every in-app browser (`disallowed_useragent`), and the Google Identity Services button falls under the same policy. Passkeys also fail there.
- **Escape:** nothing is reliable. Android `intent://` works only sometimes, and iPhone has no escape that survives app updates. So the recommended flow shows an "open in your browser" card with a copy-link button, plus a "Not working? Send me a link" fallback. `intent://`, `x-safari-https://` and `shortcuts://` are listed as try-but-don't-rely.
- **Magic link:** a one-use token held for 15 minutes in KV, with the address used to send and not stored. Opening the link restores the person's draft by session id, and they then press Continue with Google in their own browser.
- **Cost:** email needs Cloudflare's Workers Paid plan, because the free plan only sends to verified addresses. SMS through Twilio Verify costs about $0.058 per send. Plain Twilio SMS is cheaper at roughly a cent but needs US carrier registration.
- **MVP:** a detector plus the instruction card in `ux/Auth`, with no backend. The proposal also has the detector as JavaScript and a table per app and platform with credence and source links.

The YouTube row is low credence. Search sources only say its links open in YouTube's own browser, not whether it is a Custom Tab or SFSafariViewController. That matters because a Custom Tab shares Chrome's cookies and would allow Google sign-in. I did not verify whether `shortcuts://` works on current iOS either. Both need one test on a real phone, and I did not run it.

You would need to choose an email sender and add its DNS records, and decide whether SMS is worth the registration. I logged the finding in this task's `session.jsonl`.
